review_output.summary: [Medium] New MultiConnector.shutdown() fan-out and error handling have no tests
review_output.failure_scenario: No test covers the three new behaviours: shutdown reaching every child connector, later children still shutting down after an earlier one raises, and only the first exception being re-raised once all children have been tried. Nothing under tests/v1/kv_connector/ exercises shutdown. A later edit that stops at the first failure (leaking the remaining connectors' resources) or swallows the exception would go unnoticed. Remedy: add a unit test in tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py. Build object.__new__(MultiConnector) with _connectors set to three MagicMocks, the first two raising RuntimeError("a") and ValueError("b"). Assert pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="a") and that each mock's shutdown was called exactly once. Add a happy-path case too. Optionally, assert on the 'shutdown' events that TestSharedStorageConnector logs (tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/utils.py:221-251).

review_output.summary: [Low] The shutdown loop collects every exception but only raises the first, and it logs the error message twice
review_output.failure_scenario: Every exception after the first goes into a list that nothing reads, so a reader may think the errors are being combined somewhere when they are not. logger.exception already logs the message and traceback, so the extra '%s' str(e) argument prints the message a second time. Remedy: keep only the first error (first_exc: Optional[Exception] = None; set it if still None; raise it after the loop) and log with logger.exception("Exception during connector %s shutdown", type(c).__name__). If later errors should reach the caller, attach them explicitly by chaining or with an ExceptionGroup.

review_output.summary: [Nitpick] The shutdown override sits in a different section of the class than the base method it overrides
review_output.failure_scenario: In base.py:229, shutdown() is in the worker-side section right after get_finished, and its docstring says the worker process calls it. In MultiConnector it sits above the "Worker-side methods" banner, so the two files no longer line up and anyone comparing the subclass with the base has to hunt for it. Remedy: move shutdown under the "Worker-side methods" banner, after get_finished, to match base.py.
